request.text:
{"body":"## Purpose

Move the queue contract ownership to ops while preserving compatibility with edits-generated queue rows.

## Scope

- Define/host `hq.modelCommitQueued.v1`, `hq.agentTaskQueued.v1`, and `hq.receipt.v1` schema in `packages/hq-modeling-runtime`.
- Add a validator that accepts valid queue/receipt rows and rejects malformed or authority-confusing rows.
- Add valid/invalid fixtures.
- Keep compatibility with the existing edits command output shape.

## Done

- Valid model commit queue row passes.
- Valid agent task queue row passes.
- Valid receipt row passes.
- Invalid JSON, missing required fields, duplicate ids, and forbidden authority fields fail.
- Validator can be used by edits in later integration.

## Scope-achievement declaration

This issue is complete only when all of the following are true:

- Purpose lineage: directly protects editor-to-queue correctness and enables downstream ops worker/projection/ui flow.
- Core/port/adapter: schema and validation logic are pure core; validator CLI/file reading is adapter; queue IO is a port.
- Pure/effect split: row validation and error classification are pure; reading files/stdin and writing reports are adapter-only.
- False-positive exclusion: valid queue/receipt rows from known edits fixtures must pass.
- False-negative exclusion: malformed rows, authority-confusing rows, duplicate/idempotency problems, missing target when required, and invalid kinds must fail.
- Authority boundary: validator never admits or accepts rows; it only classifies intent/evidence records.
- Repo cleanliness: validator must not import editor UX or UI rendering; it is runtime contract logic only.

## Non-goals

- Do not implement worker processing.
- Do not admit rows into accepted ledger.
- Do not change Vim/hq UX.

## Checks

- Queue validator pass/fail fixture checks.
- Known false-positive and false-negative fixture inventory is present.
- Existing ops checks pass.

## Depends on

- #39

## Why this matters

This makes queue rows an ops-owned runtime contract instead of an editor-owned implementation detail."}

{"body":"## Purpose

Move the queue contract ownership to ops while preserving compatibility with edits-generated queue rows.

## Scope

- Define/host `hq.modelCommitQueued.v1`, `hq.agentTaskQueued.v1`, and `hq.receipt.v1` schema in `packages/hq-modeling-runtime`.
- Add a validator that accepts valid queue/receipt rows and rejects malformed or authority-confusing rows.
- Add valid/invalid fixtures.
- Keep compatibility with the existing edits command output shape.

## Done

- Valid model commit queue row passes.
- Valid agent task queue row passes.
- Valid receipt row passes.
- Invalid JSON, missing required fields, duplicate ids, and forbidden authority fields fail.
- Validator can be used by edits in later integration.

## Scope-achievement declaration

This issue is complete only when all of the following are true:

- Purpose lineage: directly protects editor-to-queue correctness and enables downstream ops worker/projection/ui flow.
- Core/port/adapter: schema and validation logic are pure core; validator CLI/file reading is adapter; queue IO is a port.
- Pure/effect split: row validation and error classification are pure; reading files/stdin and writing reports are adapter-only.
- False-positive exclusion: valid queue/receipt rows from known edits fixtures must pass.
- False-negative exclusion: malformed rows, authority-confusing rows, duplicate/idempotency problems, missing target when required, and invalid kinds must fail.
- Authority boundary: validator never admits or accepts rows; it only classifies intent/evidence records.
- Repo cleanliness: validator must not import editor UX or UI rendering; it is runtime contract logic only.

## Non-goals

- Do not implement worker processing.
- Do not admit rows into accepted ledger.
- Do not change Vim/hq UX.

## Checks

- Queue validator pass/fail fixture checks.
- Known false-positive and false-negative fixture inventory is present.
- Existing ops checks pass.

## Depends on

- #39

## Why this matters

This makes queue rows an ops-owned runtime contract instead of an editor-owned implementation detail."}

{"body":"## Parent

- roccho-dev/adrs#261

## Status

Evidence acquisition only. DuckDB remains the current default until the parent ADRS issue reaches an accepted state.

## Objective

Prove, by executable evidence rather than SQL translation arguments, whether a SQLite candidate can reproduce the current DuckDB-backed JSONL projection and gate behavior.

## Current boundary

The scoped runtime path currently:

```text
JSONL inputs
-> DuckDB direct read / inferred structures
-> SQL integrity and semantic gates
-> CSV / JSONL / manifest projections
```

The proof must preserve JSONL authority, generated-non-authority, source traceability, and fail-closed behavior.

## Scope

### Active execution paths

- `policy-semantic-compiler compile`
- ADRS projection review path currently named `review-adrs-projection-duckdb`
- DuckDB gate SQL
- gate CSV/JSONL generation
- detail queue JSONL generation
- positive and negative fixtures

### Read-model paths

- `find-packages/sql/projection.duckdb.sql`
- `find-packages/sql/search.duckdb.sql`

### Boundary-only paths

- `cue-append-contract-core/internal/adapters/duckdb`
- architecture checks that keep databases outside core authority

### Inventory-only paths

- historical proof output
- generated evidence
- documentation
- stale artifact names

## Required work

### 1. Freeze the current DuckDB baseline

Record:

- exact repository SHA
- DuckDB version and binary source
- Python/runtime version
- fixture and input hashes
- generated SQL hashes
- exit codes
- stdout summaries
- gate rows
- detail rows
- manifests and claims
- output file inventory
- canonical output hashes

Do not change the baseline while constructing the candidate.

### 2. Inventory all DuckDB references

Classify every reference as exactly one of:

- `runtime-required`
- `build-required`
- `test-required`
- `projection-template`
- `boundary-marker`
- `evidence-only`
- `documentation-only`
- `stale`
- `unknown`

Each row must include its caller and active reachability; grep counts alone are insufficient.

### 3. Add a minimal SQLite candidate adapter

The first candidate must do only this:

```text
JSONL
-> explicit row validation and deterministic import
-> temporary SQLite projection
-> SQLite gates
-> logically equivalent artifacts
```

Constraints:

- do not build a general schema inference engine;
- do not silently skip malformed or unknown required records;
- preserve source file, row/span, ID, and revision;
- do not create state available only in SQLite;
- do not fall back to DuckDB when the SQLite candidate fails;
- do not change the current default path.

### 4. Define parity contracts

#### Process parity

- exit code
- `ok` / `blocked`
- `candidateArtifactValid`
- `cutoverReady`
- `policyDeletionApproved`
- `generatedIsAuthority`
- gate count
- required output existence

#### Gate parity

- gate ID
- status
- blocker
- count

#### Detail parity

- missing accepted span dispositions
- missing accepted coverage
- candidate-only span dispositions
- candidate-only file dispositions
- source trace and stable IDs

#### Determinism parity

- two clean executions
- canonical row ordering
- canonical JSON key ordering
- explicit normalization of environment-specific absolute paths
- matching canonical hashes

### 5. Define an explicit engine-difference allowlist

Names may become engine-neutral, for example:

- `duckdb-executed` -> `projection-engine-executed`
- `adrs-projection-duckdb-gates.jsonl` -> `adrs-projection-gates.jsonl`
- `.duckdb` -> `.sqlite3`

Every allowed difference must be recorded. Naming differences may not conceal semantic differences.

## Mandatory counterexamples

Run both engines against at least:

1. accepted fixture;
2. missing required file;
3. malformed JSONL;
4. empty JSONL;
5. duplicate ID;
6. stale revision;
7. missing accepted proof;
8. fake proof;
9. fixture-only proof;
10. candidate-only file disposition;
11. candidate-only span disposition;
12. contradictory disposition;
13. missing source-span reference;
14. missing edge endpoint;
15. generated row claiming authority;
16. missing array field;
17. array field `null`;
18. empty array;
19. missing nested source trace;
20. boolean versus string boolean;
21. unknown field;
22. unknown required record kind;
23. engine executable unavailable;
24. identical input twice;
25. reordered input rows.

## Required machine-readable evidence

### `duckdb-usage.inventory.jsonl`

Minimum fields:

- repository SHA
- path
- line or symbol
- class
- caller
- active
- reason
- evidence

### `sqlite-parity.results.jsonl`

One row per case and engine:

- case ID
- engine
- input hash
- exit code
- status
- gate hash
- detail hash
- output hash
- elapsed time
- mismatch IDs

### `sqlite-parity.summary.json`

Minimum fields:

- baseline SHA
- total cases
- matching cases
- mismatching cases
- unresolved mismatches
- output parity
- fail-closed parity
- deterministic parity
- candidate status
- migration claim allowed

Human explanation belongs in this issue; repository proof should remain JSON/JSONL unless an existing contract requires another format.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All DuckDB references are classified.
- [ ] Current DuckDB baseline is frozen.
- [ ] SQLite candidate runs with DuckDB unavailable.
- [ ] Positive fixtures produce equivalent results.
- [ ] Negative fixtures block at equivalent boundaries.
- [ ] Exit codes match.
- [ ] Gate rows match after the explicit naming allowlist.
- [ ] Detail rows match.
- [ ] Manifest claims are not weakened.
- [ ] Unknown and malformed input fail closed.
- [ ] Two clean runs produce identical canonical hashes.
- [ ] Unresolved mismatch count is zero, or the parent remains blocked.
- [ ] The default DuckDB path has not been silently replaced.
- [ ] Clean rebuild proves the database is not authority.

## Stop conditions

Block the SQLite candidate if any of the following remains true:

- a current gate cannot be represented without changing meaning;
- NULL, boolean, array, or missing-value semantics diverge;
- a negative fixture passes only in SQLite;
- a detail queue loses rows or source trace;
- results remain nondeterministic after canonicalization;
- SQLite needs DuckDB fallback;
- a required target lacks required SQLite capabilities;
- importer implementations fragment by schema without a stable envelope;
- authority exists only in the database.

## Non-goals

- Do not prohibit optional DuckDB analytics.
- Do not touch `home` DuckLake/Parquet/WASM work.
- Do not optimize benchmark performance as the primary goal.
- Do not build a general ETL platform.
- Do not combine this proof with a broad reducer refactor.
- Do not delete DuckDB before roccho-dev/adrs#261 accepts a cutover.

## Evidence returned to parent

At closure, report:

- parity `pass` or `blocked`;
- mismatch count;
- fail-closed regression count;
- active runtime dependency count;
- remaining DuckDB-specific required capability;
- functions lost by SQLite, if any;
- recommended parent option and exact evidence paths."}

{"body":"<!-- sys1-jev-domain-entry-v1 -->
> **Domain entry:** [adrs#520 — System 1 / Jev domain](https://github.com/roccho-dev/adrs/issues/520)
> **This Issue owns only:** Jev増分効果のpaired ablation。ドメイン全体の索引・他Issueの詳細は#520へ置き、ここへ複製しない。

Refs #403
Refs #401
Refs merged #402 and #408
Refs roccho-dev/adrs#392

## Purpose

Measure the **incremental effect of Jev itself**, not just whether Jev can produce plausible semantic scores.

> A clear `NO_EFFECT` or `HARM` result is a valid and important completion outcome.

Do not require Jev to win.

## Smallest measurable question

Current intended role:

```text
candidate set
→ Jev semantic ordering
→ limited human/LLM attention
```

So the first effect test is paired and direct:

```text
same neutral cases
same top-1 attention budget

A: no semantic prior → first candidate
B: Jev ranking       → top Jev candidate

compare against runner-only gold
```

Candidate order is already reversed for every case, so the no-Jev first-candidate baseline cannot inherit a fixed position advantage.

## Metrics

For each order:

- `baselineHitAt1`: first input candidate is the gold concern;
- `jevHitAt1`: Jev top-ranked candidate is the gold concern.

Aggregate:

```text
baseline hit@1
Jev hit@1
delta hit@1
per-phase delta
pairwise reversals/ties
Jev requests/judgments
```

Result classification is descriptive:

```text
Jev hit@1 > baseline hit@1  → EFFECT_OBSERVED
Jev hit@1 = baseline hit@1  → NO_EFFECT_OBSERVED
Jev hit@1 < baseline hit@1  → HARM_OBSERVED
```

No arbitrary adoption threshold is introduced.

## Scope boundary

This first proof answers only:

> Does Jev add ranking signal under a fixed attention budget on the existing neutral cut/PR/Join corpus?

It does **not** yet claim:

- production precision;
- lower total cost;
- lower chat.pro tokens;
- lower wall-clock time;
- fewer implementation retries.

Those require a later blinded downstream-decision ablation using the same decision-maker.

## Attention comparison

Also report, but do not overclaim:

```text
no-ranking full scan = 2 candidates/order
Jev top1 review      = 1 candidate/order
```

If Jev hit@1 preserves the gold concern, this is only **potential candidate-reading reduction**, not measured LLM-token savings.

## Implementation

Do not create a new service/package.

Extend only the existing parallel-development proof summary:

```text
packages/parallel-development/
├─ proof.mjs
├─ README.md
└─ tests/run.mjs
```

Reuse the same neutral corpus, runner-only gold, reversed order, and existing envs Jev auth path.

## Acceptance

Complete when:

- effect metric is computed from the same 36 order observations;
- baseline uses model-invisible input order only;
- Jev uses raw ranked result only;
- gold remains loaded after Jev requests;
- `EFFECT / NO_EFFECT / HARM` are all representable and unit-tested;
- real Jev run retains the effect summary;
- result is attached to #403;
- no result automatically changes accept/merge authority.

## Success meaning

Success is **knowing whether Jev helped at this declared layer**, including learning that it did not."}

{"body":"## Purpose

Add the ops-owned runtime boundary for `hq.agentTaskQueued.v1` rows.

## Scope

- Read validated agent task queue rows.
- Produce pending agent-task receipts and task state.
- Ensure agent task rows are not admitted into accepted ledger.
- Leave real agent execution as future extension.

## Done

- agentTaskQueued row -> pending task state.
- pending receipt references queue id and targetRef.
- admission gate rejects agentTask rows.
- docs state agent tasks can only lead to proposals, not direct authority writes.

## Scope-achievement declaration

This issue is complete only when all of the following are true:

- Purpose lineage: directly supports agent-assisted editor-to-queue while preserving human/admission authority boundaries.
- Core/port/adapter: agent task runtime core is pure `agentTask row -> pending task + receipt candidate`; future agent execution is an adapter/runner port, not core.
- Pure/effect split: pending task classification is pure; process execution, file IO, and external agent calls are adapter-only and not required here.
- False-positive exclusion: valid agentTaskQueued rows must produce pending receipts/state.
- False-negative exclusion: agentTask rows must never admit directly; malformed or authority-bearing agent rows must fail.
- Authority boundary: agent tasks are requests only and can lead only to proposals, never accepted ledger writes.
- Repo cleanliness: real agent runners, when added later, must sit behind ports and must not enter edits or ui.

## Non-goals

- Do not run a real agent.

Add the ops-owned runtime boundary for `hq.agentTaskQueued.v1` rows.

## Scope

- Read validated agent task queue rows.
- Produce pending agent-task receipts and task state.
- Ensure agent task rows are not admitted into accepted ledger.
- Leave real agent execution as future extension.

## Done

- agentTaskQueued row -> pending task state.
- pending receipt references queue id and targetRef.
- admission gate rejects agentTask rows.
- docs state agent tasks can only lead to proposals, not direct authority writes.

## Scope-achievement declaration

This issue is complete only when all of the following are true:

- Purpose lineage: directly supports agent-assisted editor-to-queue while preserving human/admission authority boundaries.
- Core/port/adapter: agent task runtime core is pure `agentTask row -> pending task + receipt candidate`; future agent execution is an adapter/runner port, not core.
- Pure/effect split: pending task classification is pure; process execution, file IO, and external agent calls are adapter-only and not required here.
- False-positive exclusion: valid agentTaskQueued rows must produce pending receipts/state.
- False-negative exclusion: agentTask rows must never admit directly; malformed or authority-bearing agent rows must fail.
- Authority boundary: agent tasks are requests only and can lead only to proposals, never accepted ledger writes.
- Repo cleanliness: real agent runners, when added later, must sit behind ports and must not enter edits or ui.

## Non-goals

- Do not run a real agent.
- Do not auto-promote proposals.
- Do not write accepted ledger from agent task rows.

## Checks

- agentTask -> pending receipt check.
- agentTask admission reject check.
- malformed/authority-bearing fixture checks.
- Existing ops checks pass.

- #41
- #42

## Why this matters

{"body":"Refs roccho-dev/adrs#386

rel: `refined-by`

## Purpose

将来TODOとして、`ops` に存在する Cloudflare deploy authorization / account binding / provider credentials を剥離し、`ops` を credential-less provider effect implementation に縮退する。

このIssueは移管先と将来完了条件を記録するだけ。現時点ではworkflow削除・credential移動・provider effect変更を行わない。

## Target responsibility

```text
envs
  = deployment authority
  = account/project binding
  = encrypted provider credentials
  = deploy execution entrypoint

ops
  = reusable provider effect only
  = credentials stored here: 0
  = deployment meaning selected here: 0
```

## Target shape

```text
ops/
└─ packages/
   └─ cloudflare-pages/
      ├─ bin/
      │  └─ cloudflare-pages
      ├─ src/
      │  └─ deploy.mjs
      └─ tests/
         └─ e2e.mjs
```

Input is an explicit deployment request plus ephemeral credentials supplied by the caller. Output is provider effect receipt/readback only.

## Migration scope

Future migration must inventory and retire/replace all ops-owned Cloudflare credentials and credential-bearing workflows only after equivalent envs-owned execution is proven.

Do not remove an existing deploy path before:
1. envs exact deployment authority exists;
2. encrypted provider credential materialization exists;
3. credential-less ops effect primitive exists;
4. equivalent deploy + readback passes from envs;
5. rollback path is known.

## Constraints

- no provider token stored in ops;
- no account/project desired-state authority in ops;
- no duplicated Cloudflare deploy implementation;
- preserve provider effect/readback responsibility in ops;
- no broad provider abstraction before required.

status: FUTURE_TODO"}

{"body":"## Purpose

Define the CI-side HQ execution mode so issue/PR work can be shifted left without giving CI runtime authority.

## Scope

- Define `hq run ci` as ephemeral execution in GitHub Actions or equivalent CI.
- Define which local runtime inputs may be simulated or fixture-backed in CI.
- Define artifact and receipt outputs for queue validation, projection proof, preview digest proof, and cross-repo proof.
- Define stale/fail behavior when path catalog, queue schema, projection schema, or receipt schema drift.
- Connect to existing `ops#49-51` cross-repo proof issues.

## Done

- `hq run ci` mode is documented as ephemeral and non-authority.
- CI artifacts and receipts are defined as evidence only.
- The boundary between local serve and CI run is clear.
- Output receipts include enough digests to compare queue/projection/preview artifacts.
- Existing cross-repo proof issues can consume this mode.

## Scope-achievement declaration

This issue is complete only when all of the following are true:

- Purpose lineage: directly supports shift-left validation for editor-to-queue-to-ui and indirectly improves due-diligence evidence.
- Core/port/adapter: CI proof logic uses pure digest/schema/core checks; GitHub Actions and artifact upload are adapters.
- Pure/effect split: artifact/receipt classification is pure; CI execution, upload, and readback are side effects.
- False-positive exclusion: valid fixture-backed CI runs must pass even without a local long-running server.
- False-negative exclusion: stale schema, digest mismatch, missing artifact, authority claims, or invalid path catalog must fail.
- Authority boundary: CI green status and receipts are evidence only and do not create accepted state.
- Repo cleanliness: CI mode cannot require UI/editor runtime code inside ops core.

## Non-goals

- Do not replace local `hq serve local`.
- Do not promote to remote bare repo.
- Do not make GitHub Actions authority.
- Do not create an ADRS issue.

## Checks

- CI mode contract fixture.
- artifact receipt schema fixture.
- stale/missing artifact negative fixtures.
- digest mismatch negative fixture.

## Depends on

- ops#63
- ops#49
- ops#50
- ops#51

## Why this matters

The issue-based workflow is useful because CI can catch drift early. This defines that CI lane without making CI or GitHub authority."}

request.text:
{"body":"<!-- sys1-jev-issue-actions-v2 -->
> Domain entry: [adrs#520](https://github.com/roccho-dev/adrs/issues/520)
> This Issue owns only: GitHub Issueコメント → GitHub Actions → Jev評価 → 同じIssueへの結果コメント → 独立読戻し、を条件設定可能な常設機能として利用可能にすること。

## 期待状態
GitHub上の設定された対象・発火条件を満たす依頼に対し、GitHub-hosted Actions runnerで[ops#471](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ops/issues/471)の既存semlint APIを使って期待項目を評価し、同じIssueへ依頼の版・入力・評価項目・実行会計に結びついた結果をimmutable appendする。結果を独立に読戻せること。

運転は継続し、各実行は有限とする。一件の手動実証や毎回のhost操作・個別comment-ID grantの作り直しだけで完成としない。信頼された設定により対象、依頼者、発火条件、既存catalogの評価項目、呼出し上限・deadline・継続運転の予算境界、停止・再開を管理でき、同じ機能が後続の適格な依頼にも自動で作用すること。結果コメントが無条件に自分自身を再発火するloopにはしない。semantic結果からmerge/dispatch等の権限を生まない。

実行場所はGitHub Actions内。既存hostのOCI/Windowsへの接続、SSH、常設外部executor/broker、self-hosted runnerの採用を前提にしない。Jev APIへの必要な外部通信はこの境界の例外であり、GitHub内だけでJev自体を提供する意味ではない。

## 機能受入条件
- 信頼された対象・依頼者・設定とuntrustedコメント本文を分離し、対象外・権限なし・非依頼・不足/不正入力を実評価へ通さない。コメント内のref・コード・設定を任意実行や権限拡張に使わない。
- subject/contextの宣言scope・exact revision・全文と既存有限catalogへの対応を保つ。要約や欠落を勝手に補わない。
- Aligned / Closed / Unique / Minimal / Measurable / Improvingを既存catalogの範囲で評価する。未選択、context不足、実行失敗・不正証拠は成功扱いしない。
- 既存envs/opsの認証・secret供給資産を実読し、今回のActionsで使用可能な既存経路と権限を確認して再利用する。envsに鍵が存在することだけでops Actionsから使用可能と推定しない。評価用の限定された実行部だけが鍵を扱い、Issue本文・結果・ログ・artifact・一般consumerへ秘密を出さない。
- 正式entry・dirtree・供給source・Actions実行場所・非秘密設定・Issue event→executorの接続を実読できる。既存API・評価・結果検証を再利用し、実行場所固有adapterを製品の共通契約と混同しない。
- replay/重複・並行実行・作用UNKNOWNについて、実provider/postを無条件に再試行しない。各実行と継続運転の支出を有限の設定境界に収める。bot/resultの自己発火、設定変更後のstale結果、期限後・停止後の作用を成功扱いしない。
- 実Issueで依頼→Actions自動発火→real Jev→同じIssueへの結果append→独立readbackをexact source/config/input/result/runに結びつけて証明する。後続の適格な依頼でも同じ接続が動き、条件変更・非発火・失敗・重複/並行・UNKNOWN・予算/停止/再開の対照を機能範囲に比例して検証する。
- source/fixture/CI、real provider、投稿、読戻し、意味の有用性を別の証拠として扱う。mock成功、HTTP200、一回の手動実行、workflowファイルの存在だけで完成を主張しない。

## 非対象
コメントの意味・有用性の品質改善は[ops#482](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ops/issues/482)が将来consumerタスクとして所有する。既存品質系列[PR#473](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ops/pull/473)の採用・PASSを本機能の開始条件としない。新rubric、全体score、truth oracle、semantic merge gate、actor追加、DB/queue/ledger/framework、新secret/auth/IAM/Environment変更、別担当runtimeの無断変更は含めない。既存secret経路で不足が実証された場合、必要な権限境界を明示してUserへ返し、黙示変更しない。

## 既存資産と訂正境界
[PR#472](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ops/pull/472)の有限API・model/質問対応・raw Noul/coverage会計と、[PR#488](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ops/pull/488)までの採択済みadmission・結果合成・読戻し・SOURCE証拠を再利用する。各意味の正本は#471、品質の将来期待は#482であり、ここに複製しない。

以前のhost固定owner entry候補[Windows PR#46](https://github.com/roccho-dev/windows/pull/46)とPR#488のOCI内scan adapterは、既存実装・過去証拠として参照するが、今回の実行場所・発火接続・認証の前提にはしない。own認証guardを迂回してその経路を使う意味ではない。今回の完成に必要なOps非品質作業は本機能scopeであり、OCI環境不足やWindows #8全体を本機能のgateとしない。
"}

request.text:
{"body":"<!-- sys1-jev-issue-actions-v2 -->
> Domain entry: [adrs#520](https://github.com/roccho-dev/adrs/issues/520)
> This Issue owns only: GitHub Issueコメント → GitHub Actions → Jev評価 → 同じIssueへの結果コメント → 独立読戻し、を条件設定可能な常設機能として利用可能にすること。

## 期待状態
GitHub上の設定された対象・発火条件を満たす依頼に対し、GitHub-hosted Actions runnerで[ops#471](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ops/issues/471)の既存semlint APIを使って期待項目を評価し、同じIssueへ依頼の版・入力・評価項目・実行会計に結びついた結果をimmutable appendする。結果を独立に読戻せること。

運転は継続し、各実行は有限とする。一件の手動実証や毎回のhost操作・個別comment-ID grantの作り直しだけで完成としない。信頼された設定により対象、依頼者、発火条件、既存catalogの評価項目、呼出し上限・deadline・継続運転の予算境界、停止・再開を管理でき、同じ機能が後続の適格な依頼にも自動で作用すること。結果コメントが無条件に自分自身を再発火するloopにはしない。semantic結果からmerge/dispatch等の権限を生まない。

実行場所はGitHub Actions内。既存hostのOCI/Windowsへの接続、SSH、常設外部executor/broker、self-hosted runnerの採用を前提にしない。Jev APIへの必要な外部通信はこの境界の例外であり、GitHub内だけでJev自体を提供する意味ではない。

## 機能受入条件
- 信頼された対象・依頼者・設定とuntrustedコメント本文を分離し、対象外・権限なし・非依頼・不足/不正入力を実評価へ通さない。コメント内のref・コード・設定を任意実行や権限拡張に使わない。
- subject/contextの宣言scope・exact revision・全文と既存有限catalogへの対応を保つ。要約や欠落を勝手に補わない。
- Aligned / Closed / Unique / Minimal / Measurable / Improvingを既存catalogの範囲で評価する。未選択、context不足、実行失敗・不正証拠は成功扱いしない。
- 既存envs/opsの認証・secret供給資産を実読し、今回のActionsで使用可能な既存経路と権限を確認して再利用する。envsに鍵が存在することだけでops Actionsから使用可能と推定しない。評価用の限定された実行部だけが鍵を扱い、Issue本文・結果・ログ・artifact・一般consumerへ秘密を出さない。
- 正式entry・dirtree・供給source・Actions実行場所・非秘密設定・Issue event→executorの接続を実読できる。既存API・評価・結果検証を再利用し、実行場所固有adapterを製品の共通契約と混同しない。
- replay/重複・並行実行・作用UNKNOWNについて、実provider/postを無条件に再試行しない。各実行と継続運転の支出を有限の設定境界に収める。bot/resultの自己発火、設定変更後のstale結果、期限後・停止後の作用を成功扱いしない。
- 実Issueで依頼→Actions自動発火→real Jev→同じIssueへの結果append→独立readbackをexact source/config/input/result/runに結びつけて証明する。後続の適格な依頼でも同じ接続が動き、条件変更・非発火・失敗・重複/並行・UNKNOWN・予算/停止/再開の対照を機能範囲に比例して検証する。
- source/fixture/CI、real provider、投稿、読戻し、意味の有用性を別の証拠として扱う。mock成功、HTTP200、一回の手動実行、workflowファイルの存在だけで完成を主張しない。

## 非対象
コメントの意味・有用性の品質改善は[ops#482](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ops/issues/482)が将来consumerタスクとして所有する。既存品質系列[PR#473](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ops/pull/473)の採用・PASSを本機能の開始条件としない。新rubric、全体score、truth oracle、semantic merge gate、actor追加、DB/queue/ledger/framework、新secret/auth/IAM/Environment変更、別担当runtimeの無断変更は含めない。既存secret経路で不足が実証された場合、必要な権限境界を明示してUserへ返し、黙示変更しない。

## 既存資産と訂正境界
[PR#472](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ops/pull/472)の有限API・model/質問対応・raw Noul/coverage会計と、[PR#488](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ops/pull/488)までの採択済みadmission・結果合成・読戻し・SOURCE証拠を再利用する。各意味の正本は#471、品質の将来期待は#482であり、ここに複製しない。

以前のhost固定owner entry候補[Windows PR#46](https://github.com/roccho-dev/windows/pull/46)とPR#488のOCI内scan adapterは、既存実装・過去証拠として参照するが、今回の実行場所・発火接続・認証の前提にはしない。own認証guardを迂回してその経路を使う意味ではない。今回の完成に必要なOps非品質作業は本機能scopeであり、OCI環境不足やWindows #8全体を本機能のgateとしない。
"}

{"body":"## Normative status

```text
record: LOG_PROJECTED_APPLICATION_KERNEL_PROOF_001
status: IMPLEMENTATION_OPEN
parent: roccho-dev/adrs#322
reuses_internal_provider_proof: roccho-dev/ops#336
publication_owner: roccho-dev/ops#327
accepted_meaning_authority: false
production_cutover: false
customer_contact_authorized: false
marketing_mail_authorized: false
```

## Goal

`roccho-dev/adrs#322` の最小核を、一つの実装で物理実証する。

```text
append-only events
→ one deterministic reducer
→ actor/profile surface
→ permitted next action
→ POST observation
→ immutable append
→ reproject
```

同じkernelで次の二面を出す。

1. 内部面: `ops#336`でreadback済みのexact governance Release observationから、現在の内部Release surfaceを投影する。
2. 外部面: public-safeな初期value surfaceから、Web上のactionをPOST観測し、次のvalue surfaceへ進める。

## Required proof

```text
exact internal Release observation ┐
                                   ├→ same kernel/bundle runtime
public-safe external base event    ┘

external surface before
→ permitted action POST
→ one immutable R2 object
→ external surface after
→ browser reload
→ same replayed surface digest
```

### Must prove

- internal/external responses bind the same kernel identity;
- raw events and projected state are separate;
- external POST accepts only the currently permitted typed action;
- one observation is one immutable R2 object;
- repeated same request ID is idempotent;
- same request ID with different meaning fails closed;
- malformed/unknown/PII-shaped input fails before append;
- action changes the external surface without Worker/static-shell redeploy;
- internal surface is unchanged by the external subject event;
- no current/snapshot row is needed; reload reconstructs the same digest from base events + R2;
- provider readback and real Chromium bind the exact candidate SHA and deployed URL.

## Reuse / ownership

- `adrs#322`: application-kernel meaning and claim ceiling.
- `ops#336`: exact governance Release fetch/mirror/runtime-read precedent; do not reimplement its transport proof.
- `ops#327`: provider publication/readback ownership; this child does not widen ADR lifecycle semantics.
- Cloudflare Worker: HTTP observation adapter and runtime projection surface.
- R2: immutable proof observation pool only.

## V1 boundary

Use one bounded verification package under `verification/`.

```text
Cloudflare Worker + static assets
+ one R2 bucket
+ one pure JS kernel
+ one local fake-R2 test
+ one remote HTTP/Chromium proof
```

Do not add D1, Durable Objects, Queue, CRM, CDP, mail delivery, authentication, generic workflow, or a production event schema.

## Destructive cases

1. unknown profile;
2. unknown subject shape;
3. unknown action;
4. action not currently permitted;
5. duplicate request ID / same bytes;
6. duplicate request ID / different bytes;
7. arbitrary payload or PII key;
8. malformed JSON;
9. more than one semantic event from one POST;
10. R2 write not readable after completion;
11. reordered object listing changes surface digest;
12. external event changes internal subject;
13. projection/cache deletion loses state;
14. HTTP/browser failure reported as PASS;
15. technical proof represented as customer value, PMF, revenue, or cutover.

## Acceptance receipt

```text
exact_ops_base
exact_candidate_sha
kernel_identity_and_digest
semantic_bundle_digest
internal_source_reference
internal_surface_digest
external_before_surface_digest
observation_object_key_and_digest
external_after_surface_digest
reload_surface_digest
duplicate_result
negative_case_count
R2_remote_readback
Worker_URL_and_deployment_identity
browser_errors
external_requests
provider_receipt
claim_ceiling
```

## Claim ceiling

A PASS proves only that one bounded Cloudflare/R2 implementation can use the same deterministic kernel for an internal Release-derived surface and an external next-value surface, append one typed Web observation, and replay the resulting surface without storing current state.

It does not prove production authority, generic schemas, identity resolution, consent, marketing delivery, authentication, customer value, product-market fit, revenue, or corporate-sale outcome."}

{"body":"## Purpose

Connect the hq admission gate to the existing `cue-append-contract-core` append-only and validation boundary.

## Scope

- Feed accepted-ledger candidates through `cue-append-contract-core` validation where applicable.
- Prove append-only accept and rewrite reject behavior for hq accepted-ledger-shaped output.
- Emit receipts that point to both admission and CUE contract-check results.
- Keep CUE core as the contract gate, not an editor/UI concern.

## Done

- append candidate passes.
- rewrite/tamper candidate fails.
- CUE/contractcheck result digest is referenced from admission evidence.
- Existing `cue-append-contract-core` package/checks remain green.

## Scope-achievement declaration

This issue is complete only when all of the following are true:

- Purpose lineage: directly connects accepted model state to append-only contract proof and strengthens sale-ready auditability.
- Core/port/adapter: hq admission exposes a pure accepted-ledger candidate; CUE contractcheck is reached through a port; process/file invocation is adapter-only.
- Pure/effect split: append-only eligibility and result interpretation are pure; invoking `contractcheck` and reading/writing reports are adapter effects.
- False-positive exclusion: valid append-only accepted candidates must pass CUE/contract validation.
- False-negative exclusion: rewrites, tampering, non-append changes, schema violations, or missing receipts must fail.
- Authority boundary: CUE validation checks accepted candidates but does not turn queue/projection/preview into authority.
- Repo cleanliness: CUE logic remains in ops contract packages and never moves into edits or ui.

## Non-goals

- Do not redesign `cue-append-contract-core`.
- Do not move CUE logic into edits or ui.
- Do not make queue rows authority before admission.

## Checks

- hq admission -> cue append-only pass.
- hq admission -> rewrite reject.
- contractcheck adapter/core separation check.
- Existing ops checks pass.

## Depends on

- #44
- existing `cue-append-contract-core`

## Why this matters

This ties the new editor-to-queue runtime to the existing append-only contract proof without collapsing boundaries."}

{"body":"<!-- gosh-final-spec part=1/5 full_sha256=717947ab564ba83d69e6ce15d7f0be0b358538dc699d03eeb675abedde78d9ca part_sha256=c2a0435156aad348e930f4147b0cd741707007dc095fc06e0583da36ddbc7843 -->

> This issue thread contains the complete LWW specification in five ordered parts. Concatenating the Markdown content of parts 1–5, excluding only the HTML part markers and this blockquote, reproduces `gosh-final-issue.md` with SHA-256 `717947ab564ba83d69e6ce15d7f0be0b358538dc699d03eeb675abedde78d9ca`.

## Purpose

Define one Last-Write-Wins current state for `gosh` and leave the complete target architecture, the smallest mergeable v0 proof, the later promotion path, and all authority boundaries in one issue.

This issue supersedes older `gosh` design notes for implementation planning. Older issues and comments remain historical evidence. They do not need to be rewritten. A later update supersedes this issue only when it explicitly declares a new LWW current state and preserves or deliberately replaces every invariant listed here.

## Purpose lineage

| Generation | Contribution |
|---|---|
| Scope | Replace ambient shell scripts with one explicit, typed, auditable local runtime. |
| Product | Make repeatable local operations and pipelines reusable as product assets rather than hidden operator knowledge. |
| Organization | Separate authoring, resolution, execution, evidence, UI, queue, admission, and decision authority so each can be replaced independently. |
| Transfer | Let a new owner reconstruct what was intended, what binary ran, what changed, and why without relying on one machine, shell profile, person, or UI. |
| Due diligence | Provide deterministic checks, failure receipts, non-authority boundaries, and a small code surface that a buyer can inspect. |
| Meta | Turn exploratory snippets into named typed operations through a measured promotion path. |
| Meta^10 | Build a high-margin, low-operating-cost software asset whose execution knowledge is portable, auditable, and separable enough to support corporate sale. |

## LWW current-state declaration

```text
kind: architecture.currentState.v1
id: gosh-final-current-state-v1
status: current
lww: true
implementationOwner: roccho-dev/ops
authority: non-authority implementation contract
meaningAuthority: ADRS decision JSONL path
```

Rules:

1. This issue is the complete current implementation target for `gosh`.
2. Older design notes are history and rationale, not competing current specifications.
3. If an older statement conflicts with this issue, this issue wins for `gosh` implementation.
4. This issue does not overwrite `adrs#202` or create accepted decision authority by itself.
5. A later LWW update must state what it supersedes and must restate the whole current architecture; a partial comment does not silently change this contract.

## Final decision

`gosh` is a **bin-first, shell-never, local operation runtime**.

`gosh` is not:

- a new shell;
- a POSIX shell grammar implementation;
- a PowerShell object pipeline;
- an interactive REPL;
- a PTY host;
- the HQ endpoint;
- the model queue;
- the admission gate;
- the accepted ledger;
- the decision authority;
- a replacement for Nix, Coreutils, ripgrep, fd, jq, yq, or other mature binaries.

The stable division is:

```text
Go       = semantics, reduction, validation, resolution, planning, execution control
JSONL    = intent, LWW updates, provenance, and execution evidence boundary
Nix      = materializer for pinned tools where available
managed bins = mature stdio command processing
provider = operation-specific boundary for dangerous or OS-specific state changes
decision JSONL = accepted meaning source outside gosh
```

## Whole-system responsibility boundary

| Surface | Owns | Must not own |
|---|---|---|
| Herdr | Windows-local host UX, window, pane, focus, geometry | queue, admission, decision meaning, remote runtime authority |
| Vim | client/editor adapter, command and completion surface, human confirmation | worker runtime, accepted decision writes, admission, projection authority |
| `edits` | command vocabulary, targetRef consumption, human-confirmed queue writing | worker, admission, accepted ledger, projection builder, UI renderer |
| `gosh` | local tool resolution, bin execution, stdio pipelines, small native operations, snippet compilation, result evidence | HQ/model authority, UI authority, decision authority, shell/pwsh core |
| HQ endpoint / `ops` | queue validation, worker, receipt, projection, admission, source evidence, reconcile | editor UX, browser renderer, raw source authority |
| `ui` | projection reading, preview, proposal-only targetRef emission, evidence display | queue writes, command execution, promotion, admission, accepted-ledger writes |
| ADRS decision source | decision events, rules, corrections, supersessions, accepted meaning | local runtime state and generated-view authority |

`gosh` may be invoked by an HQ/ops adapter later. That does not merge `.gosh` runtime intent/results into the HQ queue/receipt/decision contracts.

## Final architecture

```text
.gosh/events.jsonl
  -> Go JSONL reader and validator
  -> LWW reducer
  -> in-memory desired state
  -> in-memory tables and tiny step DAG
  -> resolver
       -> Nix backend: installable -> outPath -> programRel -> programAbs
       -> explicit backend: declared absolute executable path
       -> later managed-artifact backend for platforms without Nix
  -> planner
  -> runner
       -> Go-native tiny operations
       -> managed-bin stdio stages
       -> compiled snippet binary
  -> all-stage results
  -> .gosh/result.jsonl
  -> promotion observation
       snippet -> cached bin -> named typed operation -> built-in operation
  -> later operation-specific provider boundary
       Plan -> approval/policy -> Apply -> Verify -> Audit
```

The two execution models remain distinct:

| Model | Use | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| bin pipeline | byte-stream processing with mature managed binaries | no hidden shell; absolute executable + argv only |
| typed operation | stable state-changing product behavior | Resource/Change/Plan/Result; side effects only in Apply |

A bin pipeline must not be disguised as an OS state model. A dangerous OS state change must not be hidden in an ordinary transform stage.

## v0 persistent layout

```text
.gosh/
  events.jsonl
  result.jsonl
  cache/
    tools.json
    snippets/
      <cache-key>/
        source/
        run[.exe]
        build.json
  bin/                 # optional derived facade; never execution authority
```

Persistence rules:

| Path | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `.gosh/events.jsonl` | canonical local input | desired local runtime intent and semantic updates |
| `.gosh/result.jsonl` | append-only evidence | what was planned/run/observed; never desired state |
| `.gosh/cache/tools.json` | disposable cache | resolved tool bindings; deletion must be harmless |
| `.gosh/cache/snippets/*` | disposable cache | compiled exploratory snippet artifacts |
| `.gosh/bin/*` | optional disposable facade | current logical tool binding; runner still records/uses resolved absolute path |

Do not persist in v0:

- `state.reduced.json`;
- `state.resolved.json`;
- compiled table files;
- a persisted DAG;
- `plan.json` managed by gosh;
- `lock.json`;
- rules/schema/migration directories;
- daemon state.

Reduced state, resolved state, tables, DAG, and plan remain explicit concepts but are rebuilt in memory on each command. `gosh plan` prints the plan; callers may redirect it, but gosh does not manage it as canonical state.
"}

request.text:
{"body":"<!-- gosh-final-spec part=1/5 full_sha256=717947ab564ba83d69e6ce15d7f0be0b358538dc699d03eeb675abedde78d9ca part_sha256=c2a0435156aad348e930f4147b0cd741707007dc095fc06e0583da36ddbc7843 -->

> This issue thread contains the complete LWW specification in five ordered parts. Concatenating the Markdown content of parts 1–5, excluding only the HTML part markers and this blockquote, reproduces `gosh-final-issue.md` with SHA-256 `717947ab564ba83d69e6ce15d7f0be0b358538dc699d03eeb675abedde78d9ca`.

## Purpose

Define one Last-Write-Wins current state for `gosh` and leave the complete target architecture, the smallest mergeable v0 proof, the later promotion path, and all authority boundaries in one issue.

This issue supersedes older `gosh` design notes for implementation planning. Older issues and comments remain historical evidence. They do not need to be rewritten. A later update supersedes this issue only when it explicitly declares a new LWW current state and preserves or deliberately replaces every invariant listed here.

## Purpose lineage

| Generation | Contribution |
|---|---|
| Scope | Replace ambient shell scripts with one explicit, typed, auditable local runtime. |
| Product | Make repeatable local operations and pipelines reusable as product assets rather than hidden operator knowledge. |
| Organization | Separate authoring, resolution, execution, evidence, UI, queue, admission, and decision authority so each can be replaced independently. |
| Transfer | Let a new owner reconstruct what was intended, what binary ran, what changed, and why without relying on one machine, shell profile, person, or UI. |
| Due diligence | Provide deterministic checks, failure receipts, non-authority boundaries, and a small code surface that a buyer can inspect. |
| Meta | Turn exploratory snippets into named typed operations through a measured promotion path. |
| Meta^10 | Build a high-margin, low-operating-cost software asset whose execution knowledge is portable, auditable, and separable enough to support corporate sale. |

## LWW current-state declaration

```text
kind: architecture.currentState.v1
id: gosh-final-current-state-v1
status: current
lww: true
implementationOwner: roccho-dev/ops
authority: non-authority implementation contract
meaningAuthority: ADRS decision JSONL path
```

Rules:

1. This issue is the complete current implementation target for `gosh`.
2. Older design notes are history and rationale, not competing current specifications.
3. If an older statement conflicts with this issue, this issue wins for `gosh` implementation.
4. This issue does not overwrite `adrs#202` or create accepted decision authority by itself.
5. A later LWW update must state what it supersedes and must restate the whole current architecture; a partial comment does not silently change this contract.

## Final decision

`gosh` is a **bin-first, shell-never, local operation runtime**.

`gosh` is not:

- a new shell;
- a POSIX shell grammar implementation;
- a PowerShell object pipeline;
- an interactive REPL;
- a PTY host;
- the HQ endpoint;
- the model queue;
- the admission gate;
- the accepted ledger;
- the decision authority;
- a replacement for Nix, Coreutils, ripgrep, fd, jq, yq, or other mature binaries.

The stable division is:

```text
Go       = semantics, reduction, validation, resolution, planning, execution control
JSONL    = intent, LWW updates, provenance, and execution evidence boundary
Nix      = materializer for pinned tools where available
managed bins = mature stdio command processing
provider = operation-specific boundary for dangerous or OS-specific state changes
decision JSONL = accepted meaning source outside gosh
```

## Whole-system responsibility boundary

| Surface | Owns | Must not own |
|---|---|---|
| Herdr | Windows-local host UX, window, pane, focus, geometry | queue, admission, decision meaning, remote runtime authority |
| Vim | client/editor adapter, command and completion surface, human confirmation | worker runtime, accepted decision writes, admission, projection authority |
| `edits` | command vocabulary, targetRef consumption, human-confirmed queue writing | worker, admission, accepted ledger, projection builder, UI renderer |
| `gosh` | local tool resolution, bin execution, stdio pipelines, small native operations, snippet compilation, result evidence | HQ/model authority, UI authority, decision authority, shell/pwsh core |
| HQ endpoint / `ops` | queue validation, worker, receipt, projection, admission, source evidence, reconcile | editor UX, browser renderer, raw source authority |
| `ui` | projection reading, preview, proposal-only targetRef emission, evidence display | queue writes, command execution, promotion, admission, accepted-ledger writes |
| ADRS decision source | decision events, rules, corrections, supersessions, accepted meaning | local runtime state and generated-view authority |

`gosh` may be invoked by an HQ/ops adapter later. That does not merge `.gosh` runtime intent/results into the HQ queue/receipt/decision contracts.

## Final architecture

```text
.gosh/events.jsonl
  -> Go JSONL reader and validator
  -> LWW reducer
  -> in-memory desired state
  -> in-memory tables and tiny step DAG
  -> resolver
       -> Nix backend: installable -> outPath -> programRel -> programAbs
       -> explicit backend: declared absolute executable path
       -> later managed-artifact backend for platforms without Nix
  -> planner
  -> runner
       -> Go-native tiny operations
       -> managed-bin stdio stages
       -> compiled snippet binary
  -> all-stage results
  -> .gosh/result.jsonl
  -> promotion observation
       snippet -> cached bin -> named typed operation -> built-in operation
  -> later operation-specific provider boundary
       Plan -> approval/policy -> Apply -> Verify -> Audit
```

The two execution models remain distinct:

| Model | Use | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| bin pipeline | byte-stream processing with mature managed binaries | no hidden shell; absolute executable + argv only |
| typed operation | stable state-changing product behavior | Resource/Change/Plan/Result; side effects only in Apply |

A bin pipeline must not be disguised as an OS state model. A dangerous OS state change must not be hidden in an ordinary transform stage.

## v0 persistent layout

```text
.gosh/
  events.jsonl
  result.jsonl
  cache/
    tools.json
    snippets/
      <cache-key>/
        source/
        run[.exe]
        build.json
  bin/                 # optional derived facade; never execution authority
```

Persistence rules:

| Path | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `.gosh/events.jsonl` | canonical local input | desired local runtime intent and semantic updates |
| `.gosh/result.jsonl` | append-only evidence | what was planned/run/observed; never desired state |
| `.gosh/cache/tools.json` | disposable cache | resolved tool bindings; deletion must be harmless |
| `.gosh/cache/snippets/*` | disposable cache | compiled exploratory snippet artifacts |
| `.gosh/bin/*` | optional disposable facade | current logical tool binding; runner still records/uses resolved absolute path |

Do not persist in v0:

- `state.reduced.json`;
- `state.resolved.json`;
- compiled table files;
- a persisted DAG;
- `plan.json` managed by gosh;
- `lock.json`;
- rules/schema/migration directories;
- daemon state.

Reduced state, resolved state, tables, DAG, and plan remain explicit concepts but are rebuilt in memory on each command. `gosh plan` prints the plan; callers may redirect it, but gosh does not manage it as canonical state.
"}

{"body":"## Purpose

Separate local queue intent from accepted-ledger-shaped output through an ops-owned admission gate.

## Scope

- Admit only validated `hq.modelCommitQueued.v1` rows.
- Reject `hq.agentTaskQueued.v1` rows from admission.
- Write `accepted.modelCommit.v1` shaped rows.
- Write `admission.receipt.v1` with ledger digest.
- Keep local/dev admission clearly separate from future production governance adoption.

## Done

- modelCommit row -> accepted row and admission receipt.
- agentTask row -> rejected/non-admitted result.
- invalid row -> failed admission receipt.
- ledger digest is stable and referenced.

## Scope-achievement declaration

This issue is complete only when all of the following are true:

- Purpose lineage: directly creates the only accepted-state boundary for editor-to-queue-to-ui and protects queue/projection/receipt from being mistaken as authority.
- Core/port/adapter: admission decision is pure core; ledger writer and receipt writer are ports; file writes are adapters.
- Pure/effect split: eligibility/admission decision and accepted-row construction are pure; ledger append and report writes are adapter-only.
- False-positive exclusion: valid human-confirmed modelCommit queue rows must admit when they meet policy.
- False-negative exclusion: agentTask rows, invalid queue rows, malformed rows, missing human confirmation, duplicate/tampered rows, or authority-confusing rows must not admit.
- Authority boundary: accepted ledger begins only after this gate; queue intent, worker state, projection, and receipt remain non-authority.
- Repo cleanliness: admission cannot be implemented in edits or ui and cannot import editor/browser code.

## Non-goals

- Do not replace future CUE/contracts admission.
- Do not make `.local/accepted-ledger.jsonl` production authority.
- Do not run real agents.

## Checks

- queue -> admission -> accepted ledger check.
- agentTask not admitted check.
- invalid queue reject check.
- valid/invalid FP-FN fixture inventory.
- Existing ops checks pass.

## Depends on

- #40
- #42

request.text:
{"body":"## Purpose

Separate local queue intent from accepted-ledger-shaped output through an ops-owned admission gate.

## Scope

- Admit only validated `hq.modelCommitQueued.v1` rows.
- Reject `hq.agentTaskQueued.v1` rows from admission.
- Write `accepted.modelCommit.v1` shaped rows.
- Write `admission.receipt.v1` with ledger digest.
- Keep local/dev admission clearly separate from future production governance adoption.

## Done

- modelCommit row -> accepted row and admission receipt.
- agentTask row -> rejected/non-admitted result.
- invalid row -> failed admission receipt.
- ledger digest is stable and referenced.

## Scope-achievement declaration

This issue is complete only when all of the following are true:

- Purpose lineage: directly creates the only accepted-state boundary for editor-to-queue-to-ui and protects queue/projection/receipt from being mistaken as authority.
- Core/port/adapter: admission decision is pure core; ledger writer and receipt writer are ports; file writes are adapters.
- Pure/effect split: eligibility/admission decision and accepted-row construction are pure; ledger append and report writes are adapter-only.
- False-positive exclusion: valid human-confirmed modelCommit queue rows must admit when they meet policy.
- False-negative exclusion: agentTask rows, invalid queue rows, malformed rows, missing human confirmation, duplicate/tampered rows, or authority-confusing rows must not admit.
- Authority boundary: accepted ledger begins only after this gate; queue intent, worker state, projection, and receipt remain non-authority.
- Repo cleanliness: admission cannot be implemented in edits or ui and cannot import editor/browser code.

## Non-goals

- Do not replace future CUE/contracts admission.
- Do not make `.local/accepted-ledger.jsonl` production authority.
- Do not run real agents.

## Checks

- queue -> admission -> accepted ledger check.
- agentTask not admitted check.
- invalid queue reject check.
- valid/invalid FP-FN fixture inventory.
- Existing ops checks pass.

## Depends on

- #40
- #42

## Why this matters

This is the line between intent and accepted model state."}

{"body":"Refs roccho-dev/adrs#388

## Purpose

ops packageの外部利用境界を `packages.${system}.<package-id>` のconsumer-ready artifactへ統一する。

consumerはops repo内部のsource path / build script / lock / asset管理を知らず、exact revision + flake package outputだけを利用する。

## First proof: hayamimi-web

現在の `hayamimi-web-build` は build/assembleを実行するCLI wrapperであり、consumer-ready distそのものではない。

新しい正規package outputでは:

```text
nix build .#hayamimi-web

result/
  = assemble.py が既に生成するHayamimi dist treeそのもの
  = static distribution可能
  = existing verify-dist.py PASS
```

属性名はprovider裁量だが、意味としては `hayamimi-web` packageのconsumer-ready artifactを返すこと。

既存 builder/CLI outputは内部実装として残してよい。consumer contractにはしない。

## General rule

今後のops packageも同じ原則:

```text
package source
→ package固有build
→ packages.${system}.<package-id>
→ $out = usable artifact
```

## Non-goals

- dist内部layoutの変更を要求しない
- ops内部のlock / asset / toolchain管理をconsumer contractにしない
- consumerごとの専用bundleを作らない
- 既存attrの改名を要求しない
- 将来commitでのattr名互換性を要求しない

## Acceptance

このIssueを実装するPRのexact commitで:

```text
nix build .#<hayamimi consumer attr>
→ success
→ result = static distribution可能なHayamimi dist tree
→ verify-dist.py PASS
```

appsはそのexact commitをflake inputとしてpinし、resultだけをconsume可能であること。"}

request.text:
{"body":"## Purpose

Keep hq queue intent semantic and machine-independent while allowing the Nix-defined envs model to resolve and place the concrete Windows provider.

The current `ops#83` proof correctly establishes:

```text
Vim -> vim-lsp -> hq.submit -> hq.hostCommandQueued.v1
    -> hq run --once -> explorer.exe -> receipt
```

This issue defines the next boundary without invalidating that proof:

```text
hq queue intent: host.open
  -> envs capability resolver: host.open provider
  -> hq runner executes the verified provider
  -> hq writes the execution receipt
```

hq must not require a second hand-maintained Windows JSONL model containing executable paths already resolved by envs/Nix.

## Purpose lineage

| Generation | Contribution |
|---|---|
| Scope | Replace machine-specific provider knowledge in hq with a typed logical capability boundary. |
| Product | Let the same hq command intent work on every realized Windows environment. |
| Architecture | Keep envs responsible for environment/provider resolution and ops responsible for execution/receipts. |
| Quality | Fail closed on missing, stale, tampered, or contract-incompatible providers. |
| Operations | Remove manual per-machine executable path wiring from hq runtime configuration. |
| Transferability | Make host-command behavior derivable from the accepted environment plan. |
| meta^10 | Reduce duplicated dependency meaning and host-specific hidden knowledge. |

## Required ownership boundary

| Owner | Owns | Does not own |
|---|---|---|
| `envs` | provider placement, provider identity, capability binding, contract version, generated registry | hq queue intent, execution decision, hq receipt |
| `ops/hq` | semantic intent, queue validation, explicit execution, execution receipt | environment dependency solving, artifact placement, machine-specific provider selection |
| `edits` | Vim client and explicit human submit | provider paths, runner, receipts |
| `adrs` | accepted architecture meaning | local runtime state |

## Scope

### Capability resolver port

Add a small hq-owned port equivalent to:

```text
Resolve(capabilityId, requiredContract) -> VerifiedProvider
```

The port result must identify at least:

- capability ID
- provider ID
- provider contract version
- executable identity or typed system-provider identity
- immutable installation/identity digest where applicable
- fixed arguments or invocation contract
- source plan/deployment identity
- verification status

The resolver adapter may initially call `envs resolve --capability <id>` or read the generated envs capability registry through a validated adapter. The port contract must not depend on registry file layout.

### Semantic queue intent

The hq queue remains semantic:

```json
{
  "kind": "hq.hostCommandQueued.v1",
  "command": "host.open",
  "path": "..."
}
```

It must not contain arbitrary executable names, environment-specific installation paths, or shell command strings.

### Execution ownership

- hq validates the queue row.
- hq resolves the required capability immediately before execution.
- hq verifies that the provider satisfies the required contract.
- hq invokes the provider directly without a shell.
- hq writes `hq.hostCommandReceipt.v1`.
- envs does not execute the queued command on hq's behalf.

### Current adapter migration

The direct Windows `explorer.exe` adapter introduced by `ops#83` remains a valid narrow proof and fallback fixture during migration.

It must be treated as one concrete provider implementation, not as permanent machine-path authority inside the hq core.

The migration must leave a clear path:

```text
current direct platform adapter
  -> capability resolver port
  -> envs-backed provider adapter
```

## Required contract for `host.open`

The first provider contract must specify:

- accepted semantic input: an existing local path
- provider behavior: open the path in the host's registered file-navigation surface
- no arbitrary executable or argument injection
- no shell invocation
- provider contract version
- deterministic validation before launch
- receipt fields sufficient to identify the actual provider and invocation

## Integrity requirements

Before executing, hq must verify:

- the queue row has not been semantically altered after confirmation
- the capability binding comes from the currently verified envs deployment
- the provider contract matches the hq requirement
- the provider identity/digest matches the registry assertion
- the provider remains executable/available
- the receipt-processing state is valid and not forged by an unrelated row

The existing queue/receipt integrity work in `ops#83` may be completed in the same implementation sequence, but this issue must not weaken it.

## False-positive exclusions

Reject:

- a queue row containing `cmd.exe`, PowerShell, or any arbitrary executable
- a provider returned for the wrong capability ID
- a provider with a missing or incompatible contract version
- an unverified or stale envs deployment binding
- a provider path that has changed since envs verification
- ambient PATH resolution that bypasses the accepted capability binding
- a queue row whose confirmed semantic digest no longer matches
- a receipt that falsely marks another queue ID as processed
- an envs resolver response that claims command-execution authority

## False-negative exclusions

Accept:

- the verified Windows system `host.open` provider selected by envs
- a managed provider installed by envs with the same contract
- a different valid provider on another target environment without changing queue semantics
- offline/local capability resolution from a verified generated registry
- repeated explicit submits as distinct queue intents
- a provider mirror/installation path change that preserves the same accepted provider identity and is re-verified by envs

## Required tests

### Pure/port tests

- valid provider resolution
- missing capability
- wrong contract version
- stale deployment ID
- provider identity/digest mismatch
- wrong capability returned
- queue semantic digest mismatch

### Adapter tests

- envs resolver command/registry adapter
- direct Windows provider invocation without shell
- missing/non-executable provider
- fixed-argument preservation

### End-to-end proof

```text
Nix envs model
  -> envs.windowsPlan.v1
  -> envs Windows realization
  -> host.open capability binding
  -> Vim / vim-lsp / real hq submit
  -> semantic queue row
  -> hq resolve provider
  -> provider launch
  -> hq receipt
```

The E2E must prove that neither Vim nor the queue row contains the concrete provider path.

## Done

- hq core depends on a capability resolver port rather than a hard-coded Windows provider path.
- an envs-backed adapter resolves `host.open` from the verified deployment generated by `envs#4` and applied by `envs#5`.
- hq remains the only owner of command execution and hq receipts.
- queue rows remain semantic and machine-independent.
- arbitrary executable, stale provider, wrong contract, tampered queue, and forged receipt fixtures fail closed.
- the existing `ops#83` host-open proof passes through the new boundary or is retained as an explicitly scoped compatibility fixture.
- Windows native E2E proves the full provider-resolution path.
- the implementation PR links `envs#4`, `envs#5`, `edits#66`, `ops#83`, and `adrs#203`.

## Non-goals

- Do not move the hq runner into envs.
- Do not make envs receipts substitute for hq execution receipts.
- Do not put concrete provider paths into edits/Vim configuration.
- Do not add arbitrary command execution.
- Do not add a shell or PowerShell core.
- Do not create a remote hq server requirement.
- Do not make generated capability registry data accepted authority.

## Dependencies and related work

- Architecture hub: `roccho-dev/adrs#203`
- Nix-compiled plan: `roccho-dev/envs#4`
- Windows realization agent: `roccho-dev/envs#5`
- Vim thin client: `roccho-dev/edits#66`
- Current hq LSP / queue / explorer proof: `ops#83`

## Merge order

1. `envs#4` freezes the capability/binding representation.
2. `envs#5` realizes and exposes verified providers.
3. This issue adds the hq port and envs adapter while retaining the current proof.
4. Cross-repo E2E records a closure receipt in `adrs#203`."}

request.text:
{"body":"## Purpose

Keep hq queue intent semantic and machine-independent while allowing the Nix-defined envs model to resolve and place the concrete Windows provider.

The current `ops#83` proof correctly establishes:

```text
Vim -> vim-lsp -> hq.submit -> hq.hostCommandQueued.v1
    -> hq run --once -> explorer.exe -> receipt
```

This issue defines the next boundary without invalidating that proof:

```text
hq queue intent: host.open
  -> envs capability resolver: host.open provider
  -> hq runner executes the verified provider
  -> hq writes the execution receipt
```

hq must not require a second hand-maintained Windows JSONL model containing executable paths already resolved by envs/Nix.

## Purpose lineage

| Generation | Contribution |
|---|---|
| Scope | Replace machine-specific provider knowledge in hq with a typed logical capability boundary. |
| Product | Let the same hq command intent work on every realized Windows environment. |
| Architecture | Keep envs responsible for environment/provider resolution and ops responsible for execution/receipts. |
| Quality | Fail closed on missing, stale, tampered, or contract-incompatible providers. |
| Operations | Remove manual per-machine executable path wiring from hq runtime configuration. |
| Transferability | Make host-command behavior derivable from the accepted environment plan. |
| meta^10 | Reduce duplicated dependency meaning and host-specific hidden knowledge. |

## Required ownership boundary

| Owner | Owns | Does not own |
|---|---|---|
| `envs` | provider placement, provider identity, capability binding, contract version, generated registry | hq queue intent, execution decision, hq receipt |
| `ops/hq` | semantic intent, queue validation, explicit execution, execution receipt | environment dependency solving, artifact placement, machine-specific provider selection |
| `edits` | Vim client and explicit human submit | provider paths, runner, receipts |
| `adrs` | accepted architecture meaning | local runtime state |

## Scope

### Capability resolver port

Add a small hq-owned port equivalent to:

```text
Resolve(capabilityId, requiredContract) -> VerifiedProvider
```

The port result must identify at least:

- capability ID
- provider ID
- provider contract version
- executable identity or typed system-provider identity
- immutable installation/identity digest where applicable
- fixed arguments or invocation contract
- source plan/deployment identity
- verification status

The resolver adapter may initially call `envs resolve --capability <id>` or read the generated envs capability registry through a validated adapter. The port contract must not depend on registry file layout.

### Semantic queue intent

The hq queue remains semantic:

```json
{
  "kind": "hq.hostCommandQueued.v1",
  "command": "host.open",
  "path": "..."
}
```

It must not contain arbitrary executable names, environment-specific installation paths, or shell command strings.

### Execution ownership

- hq validates the queue row.
- hq resolves the required capability immediately before execution.
- hq verifies that the provider satisfies the required contract.
- hq invokes the provider directly without a shell.
- hq writes `hq.hostCommandReceipt.v1`.
- envs does not execute the queued command on hq's behalf.

### Current adapter migration

The direct Windows `explorer.exe` adapter introduced by `ops#83` remains a valid narrow proof and fallback fixture during migration.

It must be treated as one concrete provider implementation, not as permanent machine-path authority inside the hq core.

The migration must leave a clear path:

```text
current direct platform adapter
  -> capability resolver port
  -> envs-backed provider adapter
```

## Required contract for `host.open`

The first provider contract must specify:

- accepted semantic input: an existing local path
- provider behavior: open the path in the host's registered file-navigation surface
- no arbitrary executable or argument injection
- no shell invocation
- provider contract version
- deterministic validation before launch
- receipt fields sufficient to identify the actual provider and invocation

## Integrity requirements

Before executing, hq must verify:

- the queue row has not been semantically altered after confirmation
- the capability binding comes from the currently verified envs deployment
- the provider contract matches the hq requirement
- the provider identity/digest matches the registry assertion
- the provider remains executable/available
- the receipt-processing state is valid and not forged by an unrelated row

The existing queue/receipt integrity work in `ops#83` may be completed in the same implementation sequence, but this issue must not weaken it.

## False-positive exclusions

Reject:

- a queue row containing `cmd.exe`, PowerShell, or any arbitrary executable
- a provider returned for the wrong capability ID
- a provider with a missing or incompatible contract version
- an unverified or stale envs deployment binding
- a provider path that has changed since envs verification
- ambient PATH resolution that bypasses the accepted capability binding
- a queue row whose confirmed semantic digest no longer matches
- a receipt that falsely marks another queue ID as processed
- an envs resolver response that claims command-execution authority

## False-negative exclusions

Accept:

- the verified Windows system `host.open` provider selected by envs
- a managed provider installed by envs with the same contract
- a different valid provider on another target environment without changing queue semantics
- offline/local capability resolution from a verified generated registry
- repeated explicit submits as distinct queue intents
- a provider mirror/installation path change that preserves the same accepted provider identity and is re-verified by envs

## Required tests

### Pure/port tests

- valid provider resolution
- missing capability
- wrong contract version
- stale deployment ID
- provider identity/digest mismatch
- wrong capability returned
- queue semantic digest mismatch

### Adapter tests

- envs resolver command/registry adapter
- direct Windows provider invocation without shell
- missing/non-executable provider
- fixed-argument preservation

### End-to-end proof

```text
Nix envs model
  -> envs.windowsPlan.v1
  -> envs Windows realization
  -> host.open capability binding
  -> Vim / vim-lsp / real hq submit
  -> semantic queue row
  -> hq resolve provider
  -> provider launch
  -> hq receipt
```

The E2E must prove that neither Vim nor the queue row contains the concrete provider path.

## Done

- hq core depends on a capability resolver port rather than a hard-coded Windows provider path.
- an envs-backed adapter resolves `host.open` from the verified deployment generated by `envs#4` and applied by `envs#5`.
- hq remains the only owner of command execution and hq receipts.
- queue rows remain semantic and machine-independent.
- arbitrary executable, stale provider, wrong contract, tampered queue, and forged receipt fixtures fail closed.
- the existing `ops#83` host-open proof passes through the new boundary or is retained as an explicitly scoped compatibility fixture.
- Windows native E2E proves the full provider-resolution path.
- the implementation PR links `envs#4`, `envs#5`, `edits#66`, `ops#83`, and `adrs#203`.

## Non-goals

- Do not move the hq runner into envs.
- Do not make envs receipts substitute for hq execution receipts.
- Do not put concrete provider paths into edits/Vim configuration.
- Do not add arbitrary command execution.
- Do not add a shell or PowerShell core.
- Do not create a remote hq server requirement.
- Do not make generated capability registry data accepted authority.

## Dependencies and related work

- Architecture hub: `roccho-dev/adrs#203`
- Nix-compiled plan: `roccho-dev/envs#4`
- Windows realization agent: `roccho-dev/envs#5`
- Vim thin client: `roccho-dev/edits#66`
- Current hq LSP / queue / explorer proof: `ops#83`

## Merge order

1. `envs#4` freezes the capability/binding representation.
2. `envs#5` realizes and exposes verified providers.
3. This issue adds the hq port and envs adapter while retaining the current proof.
4. Cross-repo E2E records a closure receipt in `adrs#203`."}

{"body":"## Purpose

Owner-only operational entrypoint for the accepted existing `graph/1`, `map/1`, and `seq/1` maxGraph App described by #233.

## Commands

```text
/mobile-agent-preset-deploy
/mobile-agent-preset-deploy-status
```

## Fixed provider boundary

- Cloudflare Pages project: `stg-mobile-agent`
- production branch: `proposals`
- App owns root routes `/app`, `/assets`, `/help`, `/protocol`, `/example`, and `/.well-known`
- Git/source provenance remains authority; Release, Pages deployment, URLs, screenshots, and receipts are non-authority projections
- no uploaded ZIP, mutable latest, second renderer, second codec, or replacement preset is accepted

## Completion readback

A successful deploy must report the immutable Release identity, deployment-specific hostname, stable hostname, full 54-file size/SHA readback, `graph/1|map/1|seq/1` resolution through the existing trusted registry, real maxGraph, and representative interaction evidence.

Architecture and adoption authority: #233."}

{"body":"# Canonical N-way attempt plan

このIssueを、今回の依頼・分担・停止条件の正本とする。candidate/resultの事実上の正本はGitHubからReadbackしたcommit/tree/blob/refとする。

## Objective / YAGNI boundary

{"body":"## Status

```text
record: OPS_SOPS_AGE_BOOTSTRAP_001
record_type: implementation_design_and_bootstrap_issue
status: ACTIVE_DESIGN_ONLY
implementation_authorized: false
key_generation_authorized_in_ci: false
key_generation_authorized_in_chat: false
secret_value_upload_authorized: false
external_effects_authorized: false
cloudflare_deploy_authorized: false
```

Refs:

- `roccho-dev/ops#104` — first YAGNI Cloudflare Pages deploy slice
- `roccho-dev/envs#87` — target/resource/deployment/secret-reference ownership inventory
- `roccho-dev/adrs#254` — proposed deployment-root and secret-reference boundary
- historical implementation: `roccho-dev/home@d02f2ea27697cc10c51724253449d0a0a3413a16/bin/src/poc/sops-flake`
- historical Cloudflare implementation: `roccho-dev/home@d02f2ea27697cc10c51724253449d0a0a3413a16/bin/src/deploy/cloudflare`

Opening this Issue records the selected bootstrap design only. It does not authorize generating keys, reading credentials, changing GitHub Environment secrets, deploying to Cloudflare, or merging `ops#104`.

## Purpose

Replace one GitHub secret per application credential with one bounded SOPS decryption identity per trust domain, while keeping every actual application credential encrypted and reviewable in Git.

Initial scope is exactly one trust domain:

```text
ops / Cloudflare / production
```

The objective is not one company-wide forever key. The objective is:

```text
many operational key/value secrets
  -> one encrypted SOPS document per bounded domain
  -> one age private identity in the runtime secret store
```

## Why SOPS is useful

Without SOPS, GitHub Environment must hold each value separately:

```text
CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN
CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID
CLOUDFLARE_PAGES_PROJECT
future provider credentials
future application secrets
```

This creates value-by-value UI administration, weak reviewability, naming drift, incomplete reconstruction and difficult rotation.

With SOPS:

```text
Git repository
  -> encrypted secret documents
  -> history, review, exact revision and rollback

GitHub Environment
  -> one bootstrap decryption identity for the trust domain
```

Benefits:

1. secret-set changes become ordinary exact Git diffs without plaintext;
2. the selected encrypted state is bound to one commit SHA;
3. missing values can be validated before effect;
4. secret names and schemas can be checked deterministically;
5. credential rotation is a new encrypted revision rather than several unrelated UI edits;
6. this conversation can manage encrypted files through branch and PR operations without receiving plaintext;
7. a second deployment can reuse the same bounded secret medium without copying values;
8. recovery and transfer require one documented key custody process rather than hidden per-value setup.

SOPS reduces secret-store entries. It does not eliminate secret authority or key custody.

## Terminology correction

The bootstrap object is not a composite key.

Age uses a key pair:

```text
public recipient
  -> safe to commit in .sops.yaml
  -> encrypts or adds recipients

private identity
  -> must remain outside Git and this chat
  -> decrypts every SOPS file addressed to that recipient
```

For CI, `SOPS_AGE_KEY` contains the private age identity. It is therefore the root credential for the bounded domain.

## Selected V1 key boundary

Create one age key pair only for:

```text
key_id: ops-cloudflare-production-v1
scope: roccho-dev/ops Cloudflare production deployment
consumers: approved ops Cloudflare production workflows only
```

Do not initially share this key with:

- development or staging;
- AWS, GCP or unrelated providers;
- customer-specific environments;
- local personal secrets;
- another repository merely for convenience.

A second key is introduced only when access, rotation, owner or blast-radius boundaries differ.

## Key generation decision

### CI must not generate the key

CI is a consumer, not the root-of-trust creator.

If CI generates the key, one of these failures follows:

1. the private key disappears after the ephemeral job and encrypted state becomes unrecoverable;
2. the private key is exported into another secret store, making CI a hidden authority-changing actor;
3. the key is logged or retained as an artifact;
4. every run creates a new recipient and makes existing ciphertext unreadable;
5. a compromised workflow can replace its own trust root.

Therefore:

```text
key_generation_in_ci = forbidden
```

### This ChatGPT thread must not generate the key

The private key must not be created or uploaded here because conversation and uploaded-file retention are not the intended secret authority, and the key would have to be returned or transferred through an unnecessary additional system.

Therefore:

```text
key_generation_in_chat = forbidden
plaintext_secret_upload_to_chat = forbidden
private_age_key_upload_to_chat = forbidden
```

This thread may receive only:

- the age public recipient;
- `.sops.yaml` without private material;
- SOPS-encrypted files;
- SHA-256 values;
- redacted validation results.

### Generate on one trusted local machine

The accountable credential owner generates the key locally or on an equivalent trusted offline workstation.

Suggested commands:

```bash
umask 077
mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/sops/age"

- universal deployment framework;
- changing accepted target or product meaning.

```text
PASS
BLOCKED_KEY_CUSTODY
BLOCKED_GITHUB_ENVIRONMENT
BLOCKED_CIPHERTEXT_INPUT
BLOCKED_WORKFLOW_ISOLATION
BLOCKED_EXTERNAL_READBACK
NOT_NEEDED
```

## Closure statement

Close only when an independent reviewer can state:

> The Cloudflare production deploy path stores complete operational key/value state only as SOPS ciphertext in the exact ops revision. One locally generated age private identity is held outside Git and injected only into the protected production job. CI does not generate the trust root, pull requests cannot decrypt production values, plaintext does not enter chat, Git, logs, artifacts, receipts or deployed content, and one ciphertext-only upload can be managed through this thread and deployed with external readback.
"}

---

## Purpose

ui#322のAtlas抽出gateを通過したLive Agent Organization Atlasを、application ownershipとしてappsへ移す。UIの再利用Parts/surfacesと意味・state正本を分け、既存の実証済み動作を保持する。

**これは移行の引継ぎIssue。作成だけで移行実装・merge・Issue close・実データ収集を開始しない。**

## 起点と開始条件

- ownership: [ui#321](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ui/issues/321)
- sequence/gate: [ui#322](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ui/issues/322)
- composition: [ui#328](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ui/issues/328)
- surface: [ui#327](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ui/issues/327)
- design/effect history: [scope PR #329](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ui/pull/329)
- **元scopeのR独立抽出gate GREEN・技術残件0:** [6009728009](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ui/pull/331#issuecomment-6009728009)
- **#331 headの自動/実操作証拠:** [6009685230](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ui/pull/331#issuecomment-6009685230)

固定した実体:
| PR | head | tree |
|---|---|---|
| ui#330 | `eb56d01d90bb20d46ad387dd72ebdd044e545316` | `8df649baf770be2385959e7505355f5a55a1fb60` |
| ui#331 | `5837cc7a856e5930350e33c68bfb73a7334ff07d` | `26a7f31fcf268678c1453b4b6cadde7a3fed9143` |
| ui#332 v4 (merged) | `769c093d507c4a3322b7a9acae2e0956680a237f` | `fd119ce3f3fa647f155f527ec836a85f3f2d70dd` |

#331は#330を直接parentとし、最終actual treeは `26a7f31fcf268678c1453b4b6cadde7a3fed9143`。#331 merge候補 `faed456dc6ebc2620ca732e6e6b3b40d0ab2dc1f` も同一treeで検証済み。
このIssue作成時点では両PRはdraft/open/unmergedだった。現在 #330/#331は実merge済みで、adopted UI commitは `f41e53c6e1afce28405dc74e27a5b77136cc9170`（同じtree `26a7f31fcf268678c1453b4b6cadde7a3fed9143`）。追加witness #332の候補と採用済みsourceは下記で区別する。実装前に必要なUI採用版と契約を確認・固定し、このIssue固有のGOを定める。後でhead/tree/contractが変わればaffected gateを再確認する。design PR #329を製品treeのparentとして扱わない。

## 移すapplication責務 — v4の境界

旧v2の「Atlas screen/read-model/projection/builder/testsを8ファイルまとめてappsへ移す」想定は、Humanのapplication-use-case訂正とv4の実source監査により置換する。画面をexampleへコピーしたりUI→apps逆依存を作らない。

| 現在の責務/path | 移行先の責務 |
